messages:
Maya Chen: Heads-up — our DLP flagged a public GitHub gist that contains what looks like a service ingestion token for svc-ingest-prod. Seen a few 401->200 transitions in the logs around the same IP.
Raj Patel: Can you paste the alert? incident id?
Maya Chen: incident #INC-2025-042, alert from runtime-anomaly-bot. Snippet: `Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX` in the gist. Source IP 89.45.210.12 calling /v1/ingest/events.
Lin Park: Oof. Steps: 1) rotate the token 2) invalidate the old token immediately 3) search logs for scope of access 4) check KMS usage and key access patterns.
Maya Chen: Agreed. I'm going to revoke the key now. Doing: `POST /internal/keys/revoke {"key_id":"svc-ingest-prod"}` via admin-runbook.
DeployBot: Revocation job queued: job_id=rb-7782 status=running
Maya Chen: Revocation completed. job_id=rb-7782 status=success. Old token shows revoked in key-service.
Raj Patel: Thanks. Can someone run a query for all successful calls using that key in the last 30 days and pull request/response hashes? Need to assess data exfil scope.
Lin Park: Running Splunk query: `index=prod_logs api_key=svc-ingest-prod | stats count by client_ip, endpoint, user_agent` — I'll attach results in the incident ticket.
Nora Alvarez: Product question — which customers use svc-ingest-prod? Samir, any CS impact?
Samir Kapoor: Quick check: svc-ingest-prod is used by customers Aster Labs and BetaCo (ingest pipeline). Both are on dedicated accounts; their data streams are separate but we need to verify no cross-tenant access.
Maya Chen: Verified no cross-tenant reads in the logs. Calls were limited to upload calls under their tenant IDs. No export endpoints used. Still treating as sensitive.
Raj Patel: Good. Action items: 1) rotate token (done) 2) verify no suspicious exports (in progress) 3) notify impacted customers with notice template (hold until we confirm) 4) rotate any CI/CD secrets that reference this key.
Lin Park: Found two CI jobs referencing svc-ingest-prod in repo infra/ci/deploy.yml — I'll open PRs to inject new token via KMS and rotate those creds.
Maya Chen: We should also add a short-term mitigation: enforce RBAC on ingest token so it cannot call admin endpoints. Who can add rule?
Raj Patel: I'll push an RBAC policy patch: deny: ["/v1/admin*"] for svc-ingest-prod. Will deploy to staging then prod within 30m.
SupportBot: Incident update: #INC-2025-042 status=containment. Notifying internal stakeholders: eng-sre, product, cs.
Nora Alvarez: For customer comms, use the minimal-impact template. Include that token exposed but no evidence of data exfil beyond per-tenant ingest, steps we took, and recommended rotation on their side if they manage tokens.
Samir Kapoor: I'll prepare the customer email draft and ping legal for review.
Maya Chen: Post-incident tasks: 1) enable retention of full auth audit logs to GCS for 90 days, 2) add a DLP rule to block tokens in public gists, 3) rotate all service tokens older than 90 days, 4) add an alert for token-use-from-new-country.
Lin Park: I'll file the infra tickets: INFRA-321 (KMS integration for CI), INFRA-322 (audit log retention), INFRA-323 (RBAC enforcement). ETA for first two: 2 weeks.
Raj Patel: Also schedule a tabletop with CS + Legal + Eng-Sec next week. Assign Maya to lead the postmortem writeup.
Maya Chen: Taking it. I'll publish a brief postmortem draft in #postmortems and link the incident ticket.
DeployBot: Deployment: RBAC policy update rolled to prod in 11m, rollback window 5m.
Maya Chen: Closing loop: revoked key, rotation completed, initial impact: limited to tenant uploads, customer comms pending legal review. Follow-ups assigned. :white_check_mark:
